newsitem.title: USA: Conrail reaches revised deal with CSX.
newsitem.headline: Conrail reaches revised deal with CSX.

text.p: Conrail Inc and CSX Corp said Friday they had reached agreement on a revised merger deal to pay Conrail shareholders $115 per share, or $10.3 billion.
The revised deal also would allow CSX and Norfolk Southern Corp, which have waged a bitter takeover battle for Conrail since October, to negotiate a break-up of Conrail's assets.

"Conrail's board and management would have preferred for the Conrail system to remain intact. However, under the circumstances as they developed, we have succeeded in negotiating the best possible transaction for all of Conrail's constituencies," Conrail Chairman David LeVan said in a statement released late Friday.

Under the deal, CSX is to raise the price and number of shares in an existing tender offer to $115 per share cash for all outstanding shares. The expiration would be set for April 18, but could be extended by CSX to June 2, 1997, meaning shareholders would be paid in less than 90 days. Stock acquired in the tender would be placed in a voting trust, pending federal regulatory approval of the deal.
CSX would be free to negotiate a division of Conrail with Norfolk Southern, but the deal is not conditional on a division agreement being reached.

Conrail said it had received assurances by CSX that there would be a "substantial commitment to Pennsylvania," with a "major operating presence" in Philadelphia as well as work shops in Altoona and Hollidaysburg and a service centre in Pittsburgh. Also, three Conrail directors would be invited to join CSX's board.
